title: Asset size threshold and regulatory burden on bank profitability

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

The most appropriate causal method for this research question is a **Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD)**.

**Why RDD?**
The core of the research question is to determine the causal effect of crossing a sharp, exogenously defined threshold ($10B asset size, normalized to `running_var = 0.5`) on bank profitability (ROA). Banks are assigned to a "treated" group (subject to additional regulatory requirements) solely based on whether their `running_var` exceeds the cutoff. RDD exploits this sharp discontinuity in treatment assignment. It compares the outcomes of banks just above the threshold to those just below, leveraging the idea that banks infinitesimally close to the cutoff are, on average, comparable in all unobserved characteristics except for

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Sharp RDD — asset threshold; test for bunching below $10B; local linear regression
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Banks just above threshold have lower ROA than just-below peers
